audit_items.title: Falsification Test: Can the roundtrip invariant coset_evals_to_cell(cell_to_coset_evals(cell)) == cell be violated for valid field elements?
audit_items.state_context: Prysm kzg.go is a thin wrapper over c-kzg-4844. Type Blob [BytesPerBlob]byte enforces fixed size at compile time. Cell cast Cell(ckzgCells[i]) is a zero-overhead type alias with no byte transformation. No caching or shared mutable state.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm's ComputeCells is a thin wrapper over c-kzg-4844. The Go type system enforces Blob size at compile time via [BytesPerBlob]byte fixed array. The type cast Cell(ckzgCells[i]) is a zero-overhead alias with no byte transformation. No state is cached; the function is pure and stateless at the Go layer.
state_anomalies_found: None at the Go layer; blob zero-padding is impossible due to fixed-size array type
If c-kzg-4844 has a bug in its FFT roundtrip, it would propagate — but this is a library-level trust assumption
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No caching present. Function is stateless.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No shared state; goroutine-safe by design.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No counterexample constructable at the Go wrapper layer. The copy is array-to-array (same size). Cell cast is a no-op. Exploit would require a c-kzg-4844 library bug.
attack_scenarios: Blob with specific byte pattern that triggers c-kzg-4844 FFT edge case — not reachable via Go wrapper analysis

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Reachable from block proposal path and reconstruction path. Blob content is attacker-supplied but field-element validity is enforced by c-kzg-4844 before cells are returned.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Attacker can provide arbitrary blob bytes, but c-kzg-4844 validates field elements and returns error for invalid inputs. No bypass at Go layer.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds by delegation. The Go layer performs no transformation that could break the roundtrip. The property is a specification-level guarantee of the EIP-4844 cryptographic library.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Go fixed-size array type [BytesPerBlob]byte for Blob; c-kzg-4844 field element validation
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient at Go layer. Library-level correctness is a transitive trust assumption.
edge_cases: Blob with invalid field elements — caught by c-kzg-4844 returning error

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The roundtrip invariant is fully enforced by c-kzg-4844. The Prysm Go wrapper adds no transformation. No vulnerability exists at the Prysm layer. A bug in c-kzg-4844 itself would be out of scope for Prysm's bug bounty.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No fix needed. Trust in c-kzg-4844 is an explicit design decision documented in the codebase.

audit_items.title: Falsification Test: Can _fft_field accept non-power-of-2 input lengths or mismatched vals/roots_of_unity lengths?
audit_items.state_context: _fft_field does not exist in Prysm Go codebase. All FFT is internal to c-kzg-4844 C library. Go wrapper accepts fixed-size Blob [BytesPerBlob]byte with no length parameter exposed.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The function _fft_field does not exist in Prysm's Go layer. All FFT is internal to c-kzg-4844. The Go wrapper passes fixed-size [131072]byte arrays with no length parameter. The type system prevents mismatched or non-power-of-2 lengths entirely.
state_anomalies_found: None; _fft_field is not exposed at the Go layer
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No FFT state or caching at Go layer.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: ComputeCells is called per-blob in parallel goroutines in ConstructDataColumnSidecars, but each call operates on independent local copies — no shared FFT state.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No path exists to trigger FFT length anomalies from the Go layer. The blob type is a fixed-size array and c-kzg-4844 uses compile-time constants for FFT dimensions.
attack_scenarios: Theoretical: calling c-kzg-4844 directly from CGo with wrong parameters — not possible through Prysm's public API

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: _fft_field is not exposed in the Go layer. The property is entirely internal to the C library. No Go code can trigger FFT length mismatches.
entry_points: N/A — _fft_field does not exist in Go codebase

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant holds trivially because the Go type system enforces fixed blob sizes and the FFT is entirely internal to c-kzg-4844. There is no gap in the guard.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Go fixed-size array type [BytesPerBlob]byte; c-kzg-4844 internal FFT sizing
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Completely sufficient. No length parameters are exposed at the Go API level.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: _fft_field does not exist in Prysm's Go codebase. The property is a specification of the underlying cryptographic library, not of Prysm's code. Completely out of scope.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No action needed. The checklist item is based on a false premise about Prysm's architecture — _fft_field is a c-kzg-4844 internal function, not a Prysm function.

audit_items.title: Falsification Test: Can the inverse FFT normalization factor 1/N be bypassed or computed incorrectly, causing ifft(fft(p)) != p?
audit_items.state_context: Inverse FFT normalization is entirely within c-kzg-4844 C library. Prysm Go layer has no FFT code. KZG proof verification (VerifyCellKZGProofBatch) provides cryptographic assurance that cells are correct evaluations, acting as independent validation of FFT correctness.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The inverse FFT normalization is entirely within c-kzg-4844. Prysm's Go layer has no FFT code. However, KZG proof verification (VerifyCellKZGProofBatch) provides cryptographic assurance that cells are correct evaluations, acting as an independent validation of FFT correctness.
state_anomalies_found: None at Go layer; normalization is C library internal
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No FFT or normalization state at Go layer.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Each blob computation is independent. No shared normalization state.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: A normalization bypass would require a bug in c-kzg-4844 that simultaneously makes ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs produce wrong cells AND makes VerifyCellKZGProofBatch accept those wrong cells. This is an astronomically unlikely scenario for a production cryptographic library.
attack_scenarios: Malicious c-kzg-4844 build with modified normalization — supply chain attack, out of scope

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The normalization invariant is double-protected: library correctness plus KZG verification. No Go-layer attack surface exists.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No Go-level API exposes FFT normalization parameters.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant holds via double protection: c-kzg-4844 correctness and cryptographic KZG proof verification. The VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData function computes cells independently and verifies them against EL-provided proofs, providing an independent check.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: c-kzg-4844 internal FFT correctness; KZG proof batch verification (VerifyCellKZGProofBatch)
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. Two independent layers of protection.
edge_cases: All-zero blob: valid, KZG verification still applies

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The normalization invariant is entirely internal to c-kzg-4844. Prysm has no Go-layer FFT code. KZG proof verification provides independent cryptographic assurance. No Prysm-layer vulnerability exists.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No action needed. The property is verified transitively through KZG proof verification.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs strictly enforce BYTES_PER_BLOB input size and produce exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and proofs?
audit_items.state_context: Blob input size is enforced at compile time via fixed-size array type [BytesPerBlob]byte. ConstructDataColumnSidecars has runtime check via copy() return value. Output cardinality is implicitly trusted from c-kzg-4844 — makeCellsAndProofs does not assert len(cells)==CellsPerExtBlob.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Blob input size is enforced at compile time via fixed-size array type [BytesPerBlob]byte. ConstructDataColumnSidecars also has a runtime check via copy() return value. Output cardinality is implicitly trusted from c-kzg-4844 — makeCellsAndProofs does not assert len(cells)==CellsPerExtBlob, only that cells and proofs counts match each other.
state_anomalies_found: Missing explicit assertion that output cell count == CellsPerExtBlob (128) in makeCellsAndProofs
ConstructDataColumnSidecars validates proof count but not computed cells count independently
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: ReconstructDataColumnSidecars uses goroutines per blob via errgroup, each writing to distinct indices of cellsAndProofs slice — safe.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Input size enforcement is robust via compile-time types. Output cardinality gap identified: if c-kzg-4844 returns N != CellsPerExtBlob cells, Prysm would not detect it and would produce malformed data column sidecars with wrong column count, potentially causing index-out-of-bounds panic in downstream indexing.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: If c-kzg-4844.ComputeCells returns K < 128 cells (library bug or CGo memory issue), makeCellsAndProofs returns CellsAndProofs with K cells. DataColumnSidecars then tries to index into cells[columnIndex] for columnIndex in 0..127, causing an index-out-of-bounds panic.
attack_scenarios: CGo memory corruption causing c-kzg-4844 to return truncated cell array — would panic at DataColumnSidecars column indexing
Malicious EL returning wrong-count proofs — caught by cellsCount != cellProofsCount check, but computed cells count is not validated

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The truncated cell array scenario requires a c-kzg-4844 library bug or CGo memory corruption — not directly attacker-triggered from P2P. Blob size enforcement from P2P is compile-time safe. The output cardinality gap is a defense-in-depth concern.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Requires c-kzg-4844 library fault or trusted EL compromise.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Input size invariant holds perfectly via Go type system. Output cardinality invariant has a gap: no explicit check that len(cells) == CellsPerExtBlob after ComputeCells. This is normally safe but lacks a defensive assertion that would prevent panics from library-level failures.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Input: type Blob [BytesPerBlob]byte; Output: implicit trust in c-kzg-4844 return value count
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Input guard is sufficient. Output cardinality guard is absent — only relative match between cells and proofs is checked, not absolute expected count of CellsPerExtBlob.
edge_cases: c-kzg-4844 returning wrong cell count due to CGo memory issue would cause panic in downstream column indexing

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The blob input size enforcement is complete and correct via Go type system. The missing output cardinality assertion is a hardening opportunity, not an exploitable vulnerability from external interfaces. Exploitation requires c-kzg-4844 library failure which is a trusted dependency. KZG proof verification provides downstream safety net.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Add defensive assertion: after ComputeCells or in makeCellsAndProofs, verify len(cells) == CellsPerExtBlob (128). This prevents panic from library-level failures and makes invariant explicit. Example: if len(ckzgCells) != ckzg4844.CellsPerExtBlob { return CellsAndProofs{}, errors.New("unexpected cell count from c-kzg-4844") }

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Are blocks with non-empty ommers properly rejected at the P2P boundary in post-merge Osaka fork?
audit_items.state_context: Prysm (CL) has zero Go code for ommer/uncle hash validation. Ommer validation is entirely delegated to the execution engine via engine_newPayload. No keyword 'ommer', 'uncle', 'OmmersHash', or 'Sha3Uncles' appears in any non-test Go file in the Prysm codebase. The delegation is intentional per post-merge architecture (CL spec section 4.3.4). During ErrAcceptedSyncingPayloadStatus, ommer-invalid blocks may temporarily enter the optimistic chain.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm (CL) contains zero Go code for ommer/uncle hash validation. The entire EL payload validity — including ommer emptiness — is delegated to the execution engine via engine_newPayload. The delegation is intentional per the post-merge architecture. During optimistic sync (SYNCING/ACCEPTED status), ommer-invalid blocks could temporarily remain in the optimistic chain.
state_anomalies_found: Optimistic sync window: blocks with invalid ommers may be temporarily accepted as optimistic (not canonical) before EL responds with INVALID
No CL-level ommer hash assertion provides defense-in-depth against a compromised or slow EL
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: ForkChoiceStore tracks optimistic blocks. An ommer-invalid block in optimistic state would be pruned once EL returns INVALID.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: notifyNewPayload is called synchronously within ReceiveBlock. No TOCTOU on the ommer check itself — the EL is the single authority.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: A malicious P2P peer submitting an Osaka block with non-empty ommers will trigger engine_newPayload on the EL, which returns INVALID, causing Prysm to call pruneInvalidBlock. The block never becomes canonical. The only exploitation window is the optimistic sync period before the EL responds.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: No full bypass found — EL always validates ommers for a well-implemented post-merge execution client. Optimistic sync window is a theoretical concern only.
attack_scenarios: Submit ommer-invalid block during EL downtime (ErrAcceptedSyncingPayloadStatus) — block enters optimistic chain temporarily, pruned when EL reconnects
Compromised EL returning VALID for ommer-invalid block — requires EL compromise, out of scope for CL audit
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Optimistic sync window: if EL is slow or unavailable, invalid block persists as optimistic until EL responds or node syncs.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Fully reachable from P2P. Any peer can submit a crafted beacon block with ommer-invalid execution payload. The rejection depends entirely on the EL returning INVALID. Prysm has no independent ommer validation.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: P2P block gossip. Crafted beacon block with execution payload containing non-empty ommers reaches notifyNewPayload and is forwarded to EL via engine_newPayload.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant is enforced by the EL, not Prysm. The guard is the engine_newPayload INVALID response path in notifyNewPayload. The guard is sufficient for well-functioning EL clients. The gap is that no CL-level ommer hash check exists as defense-in-depth. An INVALID response from the EL correctly triggers block pruning via pruneInvalidBlock.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: engine_newPayload EL INVALID status → ErrInvalidPayloadStatus → invalidBlock → block pruning via pruneInvalidBlock
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient assuming EL correctly implements post-merge ommer validation. Gap: no CL-level defense-in-depth check for known-invalid fields like ommers_hash.
edge_cases: EL in SYNCING state: ommer-invalid block enters optimistic chain temporarily
EL unavailable: block remains unvalidated in optimistic set until EL reconnects

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Post-merge ommer validation is correctly delegated to the execution layer per the Ethereum specification. Prysm's behavior is spec-compliant. The optimistic sync window is a known design trade-off, not a vulnerability. A well-implemented EL rejects ommer-invalid blocks deterministically. No Prysm-layer fix is needed or appropriate.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Informational: consider adding a CL-level ommer hash check (verify sha3(rlp([])) == EMPTY_UNCLE_HASH against the execution payload's ommersHash/sha3Uncles field) as defense-in-depth against misconfigured EL clients. This would catch the error earlier without waiting for the engine_newPayload round-trip, reducing the optimistic sync window for this class of invalid block.
